Description: A FX Swap is an over-the-counter contract between two parties made of 2 legs that can be considered 2 successive spot/forward transactions. A Near Leg: the two parties agree to exchange one currency against another at an initial date (First Value Date) for a first exchange rate. A Far Leg: the two parties agree to exchange back the same currencies at a future date compared to initial date (Second Value Date) for a second exchange rate. The difference between the exchange rate applied on near and far leg reflects the interest differentials between the two  currencies concerned, also called swap points.
